subject: SLO & throughput follow-up — streaming concurrency sampling and bench plan
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimblecart.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLOs, peak vs steady, and streaming needs — follow-up

Thanks for the call earlier, Alex — good alignment. Short recap and concrete asks so we can size and propose a pilot: 

1) High-level SLO targets you mentioned
   - Interactive streaming (chat-like): P95 end-to-end latency target <= 350 ms for token delivery (client-visible).
   - Non-streaming completion calls: P95 <= 200 ms to first token, P99 <= 500 ms to full response (aspirational).

2) Throughput profile (your numbers from the call) — please confirm:
   - Steady-state: ~40 QPS of completion requests (avg), average request ~300 tokens.
   - Peak crests: up to ~10x above baseline for short windows (we heard ~400 QPS sustained for sub-60s spikes).
   - Concurrent streaming sessions: ~250 active streams during peak windows.

Converted metrics we will size against:
   - Steady tokens/sec ~= 40 QPS * 300 tokens = 12,000 tokens/sec.
   - Peak tokens/sec (worst-case) ~= 400 QPS * 1,200 tokens = 480,000 tokens/sec (if long requests hit at peak).

3) Workload nuance we need from you (action items):
   - Shared sample payloads: ~500–1,000 representative requests (JSONL) across short/medium/long conversations — include timestamps, avg tokens, and whether streaming or one-shot.
   - Tail session distribution: percent of sessions that exceed 1k tokens, 2k tokens.
   - Typical session duration and inter-token cadence for streaming (client-sent prompts vs server-sent tokens).

4) Redwood offers:
   - We can run a 48-hour staging pilot with traffic replay (non-prod) and capture per-token latency percentiles and KV-cache behavior.
   - We'll provide an ops-friendly dashboard (token/sec, concurrency heatmap, P50/P95/P99) and a proposed autoscale/burst configuration.

Next steps / asks: please upload the sample payloads and a short SLO doc to the Drive link below by EOD Friday so Karthik can complete the sizing math and we can propose a pilot scope.

Attachments: nimblecart_sample_payloads.jsonl (placeholder), nimblecart_expected_slas.xlsx

Thanks — I'll coordinate an internal sizing readout once we have the files.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimblecart.com>

Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLOs, peak vs steady, and streaming needs — follow-up

Thanks, Rachel — appreciate the summary. Quick confirmations and clarifications from our side: 

- The SLOs you captured match what we discussed (P95 streaming ~350ms). We'll flag any internal constraints if our security team pushes back.
- Payloads: we'll provide 750 sample requests (mix JSONL + a short spreadsheet with token counts).
- Average tokens/request: ~300 typical; long-horizon conversations ~1k–1.2k tokens (happen ~6–8% of traffic).
- Peak behavior: peaks are caused by marketing-triggered campaigns; crests typically last 30–90s, roughly 10x baseline.
- Streaming model: we stream model tokens back as they are produced (server push) and client renders them; most calls send the entire prompt upfront.

I'll upload the files to the Drive folder and loop our ops email (ops@nimblecart.com) for any additional telemetry. We should be able to get these to you by Thu EOD.

— Alex
Alex Turner
Head of Product, NimbleCart
alex.turner@nimblecart.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimblecart.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLOs, peak vs steady, and streaming needs — follow-up

Alex — thanks for the quick turnaround on numbers. A couple of technical clarifications that will materially affect capacity sizing and the pilot configuration: 

1) Tokenization and measurement
   - Please confirm which tokenizer you use (we need to know whether your token counts are byte-pair or tokenized via tiktoken-like scheme). If you can't, provide raw character counts and a small mapping sample.

2) Streaming cadence and per-token size
   - When you say "server push" streaming, is the typical token emission bursty (e.g., many tokens in <50ms) or steady (one token every 10–30ms)? The shape changes memory/KV cache pressure.

3) Tail / long-session frequency
   - You noted 6–8% of requests go above 1k tokens. Please provide the percentile breakpoints (50/90/95/99) for tokens per request and for session length in seconds.

4) Proposed sampling plan (what we need to size properly) — please provide in the shared Drive: 
   - 1,000 request traces (JSONL) sampled across peak and steady windows, with timestamps, token count, and whether streaming was used.
   - A few full streaming traces (server-side timestamps per token) for 30–50 longer sessions so we can compute per-token latency distribution.

Initial sizing note (back-of-envelope) — assuming t = tokens, q = QPS:
   - Steady: q=40, t_avg=300 => tokens/sec ~= 12k (baseline)
   - Peak crest: q=400, t_avg=1200 => tokens/sec ~= 480k (worst-case)
   - If long-horizon sessions cluster at crest, we need to capacity-plan for sustained memory/KV cache pressure not just raw GPU token throughput.

We can also run a small internal replay of a 2-hour window to sanity-check tail behavior once you drop the traces. That will inform recommended batching/quantization and an autoscale burst runway.

Ping me when the Drive link is live — I'll carve out time Thu/Fri to run the quick replay and get back with an ops-oriented pilot scope.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

- Karthik / Redwood: run a 2-hour replay and provide a short ops readout (heatmaps + recommended burst runway) by Fri (2027-05-14).
- Rachel / Redwood: draft pilot scope (48-hr staging replay + telemetry + a single-week pilot runbook) and share by Mon (2027-05-17).

If any of these dates are tight, flag now and we'll shift. We'll also include an optional 1-hour technical kickoff next week (suggest Tue/Thu morning PT) to walk the pilot checklist.

Attachments: redwood-staging-pilot-checklist.pdf

Thanks all — looking forward to the traces.

— Rachel
